response.justification: The candidate is an experienced generalist software engineer with strong web, backend, and D/TypeScript credentials, but the role's mandatory requirements are largely unmet. C++ exposure is limited to roughly six months at National Instruments (2014–2015) plus a university thesis project — far short of the required 5–10 years of hands-on C++. There is no evidence of Windows-platform development, no SQL Server or Oracle experience (only generic SQL/MySQL/MongoDB), and no fixed income, capital markets, or investment banking domain background. The one adjacent experience, RIDE Capital, is retail investment fintech built in Node/TypeScript, not capital-markets C++ systems. Strong engineering fundamentals and communication skills are evident, but they do not compensate for the absence of every mandatory criterion.
strengths: Deep engineering fundamentals: TDD, CI/CD, low-latency systems, high-throughput microservices
Excellent communication — public speaker, workshop creator, course author, open-source maintainer
Broad polyglot adaptability across systems, backend, and infrastructure work
concerns: Only ~6 months of professional C++, over a decade ago; no recent systems-language depth
No fixed income, derivatives, or investment banking/capital markets domain experience
No SQL Server/Oracle or Windows-platform development evidence; stack is Linux/web-centric
